intro_html: Pork braised low and slow in tomatoes and mirepoix until it shreds with a look, then piled over ribbons of pasta. Sounds like a $30 trattoria plate; it is actually about $1.26 a bowl with 37 grams of protein and 578 calories. Time does the work, and time is free.
cost_closing_html: About $1.26 a bowl for a slow-braised pork ragu that restaurants price like a car payment appetizer.
shop_smart: Pork loin at around $2 a pound is the whole reason this batch is so cheap. Whole loins go on deep sale often; buy one, cube half for this, freeze the rest.
Carrots, celery, and onion are the cheapest flavor base in cooking. Buy whole carrots and a full celery bunch, not the pre-cut cups, and you pay a third the price.
We use fettuccine instead of pappardelle because it is the same egg-noodle idea at a fraction of the cost per ounce. Nobody can tell under a ladle of ragu.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Cut the pork loin into 2-inch chunks and season with salt and pepper. Heat the vegetable oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high and sear the pork in batches until browned on a couple of sides. Set aside.
In the same pot, cook the diced onion, carrots, and celery for 5 to 6 minutes until softened, then add the garlic and tomato paste and stir 1 minute.
Pour in the beef broth and diced tomatoes, scraping up the browned bits. Add the thyme and Italian seasoning, then return the pork and its juices.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and braise on low heat (or in a 300F oven) for 2 to 2.5 hours, until the pork shreds easily with a fork.
Shred the pork right in the pot with two forks and simmer uncovered 10 to 15 minutes to thicken the sauce. Taste for salt.
Boil the fettuccine in salted water to al dente, drain, and fold it into the ragu until every ribbon is coated.
portion_html: Set the loaded pot on the scale, subtract the empty-pot weight, and divide by 14. Twirl even portions into 14 containers; the sauce keeps the pasta from drying out all week. Each bowl lands at 578 calories and 37 grams of protein.

head.description: Slow-braised pork ragu meal prep over pasta ribbons, built on cheap pork loin and mirepoix. 578 calories, 37g protein, about $1.26 per serving.
head.keywords: pork ragu, braised pork pasta, pappardelle ragu, budget meal prep, slow braised pork, cheap high protein dinners
steps: Cube and season the pork, then sear it in batches in a Dutch oven.
Soften the onion, carrots, and celery, then stir in garlic and tomato paste.
Add broth, diced tomatoes, and herbs, return the pork, and braise covered on low 2 to 2.5 hours.
Shred the pork in the pot and simmer uncovered to thicken.
Boil the fettuccine, fold it into the ragu, and portion into 14 containers.
